Last September I finally visited the town my grandmother talked about all her life. I took an early bus and arrived before the shops opened. The streets were empty, and the light on the old stone was stunning. I walked for two hours without a map. At noon I found a small square behind the cathedral, and I sat there with a coffee and a piece of cake. An old woman asked me where I was from, and we talked for twenty minutes. I understood almost everything she said. I did not want to leave. It was a short trip, but it was unforgettable.

Good morning, everyone. Before we walk down to the water, let me tell you how this harbor began. Fishermen built the first houses here more than eight hundred years ago. In the fifteenth century the town grew rich, and the families paid for the church you see on your right. Then, in sixteen sixty-seven, a strong earthquake destroyed almost everything. The people did not leave. They rebuilt the same streets, with the same stone, and they finished the work in less than thirty years. That is why the old town still looks medieval today.

They arrived in Split late at night and found a small door in a wall. In the morning they walked on cobblestone streets between medieval houses. At eleven they sat down in a cafe near the harbor and watched the fishing boats. An old man at the next table told them where to eat. That evening the town became lively and they ate grilled fish by the water.
